answer.lead: You can carry over up to 5 unused PTO days into next year. I stopped looking early because I hit the tool limit for this turn, but I had the policy text I needed.

policy_facts.text: The standard carryover cap is 5 unused PTO days into the next calendar year. Unused days above 5 are forfeited on December 31 and are not paid out.

citations.snippet: You can carry over up to 5 unused PTO days into the next calendar year.

policy_facts.text: If you are on approved leave that spans December 31, such as parental leave, the cap is 10 days instead of 5. This is applied automatically when the leave is recorded in the HR Portal.

citations.snippet: If you are on approved leave that spans December 31, you can carry over up to 10 unused PTO days instead of 5.

recommendations.text: If you take no more PTO before December 31, you would have 11.0 days unused. That is about 6 days over the 5-day cap, and those days would be forfeited. Consider scheduling time off before year-end, and check the HR Portal's expected carryover figure.
If you plan a leave that spans December 31, ask HR whether the 10-day cap applies. I can open an HR ticket if you'd like.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
You can carry over up to 5 unused PTO days into the next calendar year. On December 31, any unused days above the 5-day cap are forfeited.
Forfeited days are not paid out. The HR Portal shows your expected carryover from the autumn onwards, so you can plan to use the rest of your PTO before the end of the year. Carried-over days appear in your balance on January 1 and are used like any other PTO.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
If you are on approved leave that spans December 31, you can carry over up to 10 unused PTO days instead of 5.
This applies to approved leave under the Leave of Absence Policy, such as parental leave, that is in progress on December 31. It is applied automatically when your leave is recorded in the HR Portal; you don't need to request it.

passages.text:
If you leave Ridgeline, any payout of unused PTO is handled by HR at separation.
Plan your remaining PTO with your manager once you have given notice; approved PTO in your notice period is taken as normal. HR confirms your final balance and how it is handled in your final pay. Questions about your own situation go to the HR Service Desk.
